notes: kb/Work/PB423.md LANDED - SR1's whole closed class list is now enforced in BOTH operand positions. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.25.3 'The class of identifier-1 or identifier-2 shall not be index, message-tag, object, or pointer.' -> OK, 14.9.25.3 1). THE INDEX ARM was already complete (kb/Work PB124/PB416) and is unchanged. THE POINTER AND OBJECT ARMS WERE ABSENT, excused by an in-code comment asserting that 'message-tag/object/pointer classes cannot reach a bound MOVE yet (their usages are compile-gated skeletons, W2 track B)' - a premise PicInfo's own XML docs contradicted (Usage.Pointer 'LIVE (Phase-4b increment 1)', Usage.ProgramPointer 'LIVE (P10 Step 7)', Usage.ObjectReference 'LIVE (the Phase-3 OO spine)') and conformance:cases/13.18.5-BASED/based_pointer disproved end to end. MEASURED BEFORE at --std 2023 and --std 2002 alike: MOVE P TO Y (a USAGE POINTER sender into PIC X(8)) compiled, ran and printed Y=[WiseOwl.Cobol] - the CLR type name of the pointer carrier, deposited into a user's alphanumeric item with no diagnostic; MOVE NULL TO P reached Roslyn and surfaced 'error CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type string to WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime.ManagedPointer', a message about GENERATED C#, in place of a COBOL diagnostic; MOVE P TO Q, MOVE R TO S (program-pointers) and MOVE G TO H (object references) were accepted silently. AFTER: every one draws COBOL0809 in each offending position. THE SHAPE, and it is the two-arm one: SR1 is ONE sentence about 'identifier-1 OR identifier-2', and the sending arm had already been routed through the 8.5.2.1 Table-2 class reader while the receiving arm still pattern-matched one hand-written usage (t.Item.Pic is { Usage: Usage.Index }). Both now call one private core, MoveTable16.Sr1ClassRefusal, over IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf / ClassOfPlace - so class POINTER spans all three of its 8.5.2.1 Table 2 categories (data-pointer, function-pointer, program-pointer) where a usage test would have missed FUNCTION-POINTER exactly as the old one missed the others. The refusal text names the class and the rule the programmer wants instead (13.18.60.3 SR9/SR8 for the pointers, SET for an object reference). MESSAGE-TAG has no CobolClass member and needs none: the MCS facility is declined (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 4) and PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage refuses the usage by name (COBOL1943), so no operand of that class can be bound - MoveOperandClassDriftTests asserts that EVERY usage 13.18.60.3 SR4 names (the six that produce SR1's four classes) is refused in both positions with the same text, and that a usage with no bound PicInfo answers null in both, so the moment MESSAGE-TAG gains a model the test fails rather than the screen silently narrowing. The complement is pinned too: conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb423_move_operand_class_admitted declares the very items SR1 bars and references them only where 13.18.60.3 SR9 and 8.8.4.2.16 admit them, so a widening of the class list shows up as a red rather than as rejected legal source. || TRAIN-39 COMPOSITION REPAIR (the lander, not either implementer): PB423's batch wrote the MoveBinder site as MoveFigurativeEditionGates, the name it carried on PB423's base; PB425's finisher RENAMED that method MoveOperandClassChecks in the same train, because what is left in it after the StoreAsImage marking moved to MarkFillImageStorage IS this rule and nothing else.
